```{r}
#| label: setup-shared
#| include: false
# The setup that the segments without a case need: packages, the palette of
# style/cgm-slides.scss, the slide theme, the repeatability matrix, the 29
# red-card estimates and the number formats. Every figure is drawn here or in
# its segment from data files or from small tribbles of published values,
# never from an image of a published figure. Relative paths resolve from
# slides/ at render time. The setup of a case comes after this chunk and may
# use everything defined in it; it must define case_vars, the entry of the
# case under cases: in _variables.yml, whose addresses the shared segments
# print (the workspace on the tools slide of Part 1).
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(purrr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork)
})

ncl_blue <- "#0e3b6a"
orange   <- "#E69F00"
green    <- "#009E73"
d_red    <- "#a10000"
grey_mid <- "#848c94"
burgundy <- "#8b1538"
ink      <- "#1d2733"

# A light slide theme: large type and no chart-junk.
theme_slide <- function(base_size = 17) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey90"),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = ncl_blue),
      axis.title = element_text(colour = ncl_blue),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
}

# Numbers in slide text: a true minus sign and fixed decimals, shares in per
# cent, thousands with a comma.
fmt_num <- \(x, d = 3) sub("^-", "−", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d))
fmt_pct <- \(x, d = 1) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = d), "%")
fmt_n <- \(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
fmt_signed <- \(x, d = 1) paste0(if_else(x > 0, "+", ""), fmt_num(x, d))

# The four cells of the repeatability matrix (Nosek et al. 2025), with the
# definitions of the glossary. The full-colour slide and any emphasis slide
# draw from this one table.
repeatability_cells <- tribble(
  ~analysis,           ~data,            ~term,              ~def,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              ~fill,
  "SAME METHODS",      "SAME DATA",      "Reproducibility",  "Testing the reliability of a prior finding\nwith the same data and same analysis\nstrategy by comparing the outcome of an\ninferential test as reported in a paper\nwith a re-calculation of that inferential\ntest from the original data.", "#0e3b6a",
  "DIFFERENT METHODS", "SAME DATA",      "Robustness",       "Testing the reliability of a prior finding\nwith the same data and different analysis\nstrategy by conducting alternative\ntests on the original data.",                                                                           "#E69F00",
  "SAME METHODS",      "DIFFERENT DATA", "Replicability",    "Testing the reliability of a prior finding\nwith new data expected to be theoretically\nequivalent by comparing the outcome of an\ninferential test as reported in a paper\nwith the equivalent inferential test as\ncalculated in the new dataset.", "#009E73",
  "DIFFERENT METHODS", "DIFFERENT DATA", "Generalisability", "Testing the reliability of a prior finding\nin a new dataset in a way that differs\nfrom the original study but is expected\nto produce similar results.",                                                                         "#834848"
)

# `highlight = NULL` keeps all four cells in colour; a term (e.g.
# "Robustness") dims every other cell to light grey.
repeatability_matrix <- function(highlight = NULL) {
  grey_box <- "#b6bcc3"
  cells <- repeatability_cells |>
    mutate(
      data = factor(data, levels = c("SAME DATA", "DIFFERENT DATA")),
      analysis = factor(analysis, levels = c("DIFFERENT METHODS", "SAME METHODS")),
      fill = if (is.null(highlight)) fill else if_else(term == highlight, fill, grey_box)
    )
  ggplot(cells, aes(data, analysis)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = fill), colour = "white", linewidth = 4, width = 1, height = 1) +
    geom_text(aes(label = term), colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 9, nudge_y = 0.25) +
    geom_text(aes(label = def), colour = "white", size = 5, nudge_y = -0.1, lineheight = 0.95) +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_void(20) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text = element_text(face = "bold", colour = ncl_blue),
          axis.text.x.top = element_text(size = 17),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 15, angle = 90, hjust = 0.5),
          plot.margin = margin(2, 8, 2, 2))
}

# The 29 teams of Silberzahn et al. (2018), published values, read once
# because two slides in different parts draw them. The file is shared by the
# decks of every case; codebook: data/silberzahn29_codebook.md.
silberzahn29 <- read_csv("../data/silberzahn29.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(distribution = factor(distribution, levels = c("Linear", "Logistic", "Poisson", "Other")))

# The teams capitalised their methods 29 ways; the published table
# title-cases them, and the forest slide follows suit.
tidy_approach <- function(x) {
  stringr::str_replace_all(stringr::str_to_title(x),
                           "\\b(And|A|For|With|Using|The|Of)\\b", tolower)
}
```
